items.title: Teach AI What It Doesn't Know
items.abstract: Abstract AI systems are rapidly transitioning from laboratory demonstrations to decision‐making technologies deployed in high‐stakes domains. Yet reliability remains a primary obstacle to responsible adoption: discriminative models can be confidently wrong under out‐of‐distribution (OOD) inputs, and foundation models (FMs) such as large language models (LLMs) can generate fluent but untruthful, harmful, or misaligned outputs. My research develops the foundations of reliable machine learning with minimal human supervision , unifying algorithms, and theory that make reliability a first‐class objective alongside accuracy. I advance unknown‐aware learning through automated outlier generation, introducing feature‐ and input‐space synthesis frameworks that regularize decision boundaries and improve interpretability. I further establish principled methods for learning “in the wild” by leveraging unlabeled deployment data under mixture and contamination models, with theoretical guarantees and state‐of‐the‐art performance for OOD detection and generalization under diverse shifts. Finally, I design reliability frameworks for FMs by exploiting unlabeled signals to detect hallucinations, defend against malicious prompts in vision–language models, and denoise noisy preference data for more dependable alignment. Collectively, these contributions provide a cohesive toolkit for deploying AI systems that remain accurate, calibrated, and trustworthy in open‐world environments.

items.title: Teacher Support, AI Literacy, Personal Best Goals, and Engagement in AI ‐Supported English Learning: A Goal‐Setting Theory Perspective
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into English language education has generated growing interest in understanding engagement in AI‐supported learning environments, particularly in vocational education contexts. Drawing on goal‐setting theory, this study examined the associations among teacher support, AI literacy, personal best goals, and engagement in AI‐supported English learning among vocational college students. Data were collected from 573 Chinese vocational college students with prior experience in AI‐assisted English learning. Structural equation modelling was employed to test the hypothesized relationships and mediating effects. The results indicated that teacher support and AI literacy were positively associated with personal best goals and engagement. Personal best goals were positively associated with engagement and served as a motivational correlate linking teacher support and AI literacy with engagement. By focusing on vocational college students, this study fills a critical gap in research on their engagement in AI‐supported language learning, informing the design of AI‐Supported vocational English instruction.

items.title: Teacher-Student Relationships in the AI Era
items.abstract: The relationships between teachers and students are essential to quality education. As A.I. is more and more woven into educational practice, these relationships are being configured in ways that go beyond efficiency of instruction. Examine how AI-mediated educational environments influence the trust, dialogue, and human bonding targets of teacher-student relationships in the AI era. Through the lens of relational and ethical theories of education, AI is conceptualized as a sociotechnical mediator rather than a neutral/moral agent. The examination illustrates that algorithmic authority can destroy relational trust while the simulated interaction obscures the ethical grounding of pedagogical dialogue and over-automation threatens the loss of emotional presence and care. In response, the research forwards a human-centered relational framework that situates AI as an augmentative aid supporting rather than supplanting human judgment, dialogic engagement, and human bonding, and outlines implications for practice, teacher education, and policy.

items.title: Teaching and Learning in the Age of AI: Reversed Bloom’s Taxonomy, Relational Teaching, and Socially Engaged Pedagogy
items.abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into higher education has raised concerns about academic integrity, assessment validity, and quality assurance. This case study addresses these concerns from a pedagogical design perspective, arguing that sustaining meaningful engagement in AI-pervasive contexts requires intentional alignment among assessment structure, relational teaching practices, and socially engaged pedagogy. Drawing on Rivers and Holland’s (2023) Reversed Bloom’s Taxonomy and relational theories of education (Biesta, 2004), the study introduces a teaching approach that begins with higher-order cognitive processes and positions the teacher–student relationship as instrumental in achieving learning outcomes. Relational teaching principles—understanding student context, building trust, fostering connection, and offering structured support—are embedded throughout course design. A central component of this intentional design is the integration of The HistoryMakers Digital Archive (THMDA) as socially engaged pedagogy. By grounding inquiry in lived narratives and plural perspectives, THMDA anchors learning in real-world contexts and human experience. The case study illustrates how this integrated approach is operationalized through course assignments structured around three core commitments: equity and inclusion, student co-construction of meaning, and real-world relevance. Assignments prioritize creation, interpretation, dialogue, and contextual judgment rather than content reproduction. Preliminary evidence from course implementation indicates increased student engagement, stronger theoretical application, greater transparency in AI use, and deeper reflective learning. The study contributes a practical, human-centered model demonstrating how reversed assessment design, relational pedagogy, and intentional use of socially engaged knowledge sources can support innovation and transformative learning in contemporary higher education.

items.abstract: The utilization of artificial intelligence tools to assist teaching has become the norm in many classroom settings, particularly in higher education course instruction. This paper addresses the critical issues existing in operations research teaching, as well as the current status of teaching methodologies in higher education institutions. It investigates the application of problem-based learning (PBL) methods in the "Operations Research" curriculum, designs a systematic structure for the PBL teaching model in "Operations Research" by integrating AI assistants provided by teaching platforms, and implements classroom instruction based on specific case studies. The research demonstrates that implementing AI-assisted PBL teaching methods in operations research instruction can alleviate non-mathematics majors' resistance to fundamental mathematical content, stimulate their enthusiasm for knowledge exploration, enhance students' autonomous learning capabilities, and improve the efficiency and quality of problem-solving.

items.title: Teaching Strategies for Active Engagement and Collaboration in Online Courses
items.abstract: The digital transformation of education has redefined the way learners engage with content, instructors, and peers in virtual classrooms. Engagement and collaboration are pivotal in ensuring knowledge retention, learner satisfaction, and academic achievement in online learning environments. This chapter explores the dimensions of online engagement behavioral, cognitive, and emotional and examines the role of group collaboration in fostering active participation, critical thinking, and social interaction. It highlights the pedagogical models, technological tools, and instructional strategies that enhance collaborative learning while addressing the challenges of virtual teamwork. Practical insights and case studies illustrate best practices for promoting inclusivity, motivation, and equal participation. The chapter concludes by discussing future directions in online engagement, including the integration of artificial intelligence, learning analytics, and immersive technologies, to create more personalized and interactive digital classrooms.

items.title: The Accountability Horizon: An Impossibility Theorem for Governing Human-Agent Collectives
items.abstract: Existing accountability frameworks for AI systems, legal, ethical, and regulatory, rest on a shared assumption: for any consequential outcome, at least one identifiable person had enough involvement and foresight to bear meaningful responsibility. This paper proves that agentic AI systems violate this assumption not as an engineering limitation but as a mathematical necessity once autonomy exceeds a computable threshold. We introduce Human-Agent Collectives, a formalisation of joint human-AI systems where agents are modelled as state-policy tuples within a shared structural causal model. Autonomy is characterised through a four-dimensional information-theoretic profile (epistemic, executive, evaluative, social); collective behaviour through interaction graphs and joint action spaces. We axiomatise legitimate accountability through four minimal properties: Attributability (responsibility requires causal contribution), Foreseeability Bound (responsibility cannot exceed predictive capacity), Non-Vacuity (at least one agent bears non-trivial responsibility), and Completeness (all responsibility must be fully allocated). Our central result, the Accountability Incompleteness Theorem, proves that for any collective whose compound autonomy exceeds the Accountability Horizon and whose interaction graph contains a human-AI feedback cycle, no framework can satisfy all four properties simultaneously. The impossibility is structural: transparency, audits, and oversight cannot resolve it without reducing autonomy. Below the threshold, legitimate frameworks exist, establishing a sharp phase transition. Experiments on 3,000 synthetic collectives confirm all predictions with zero violations. This is the first impossibility result in AI governance, establishing a formal boundary below which current paradigms remain valid and above which distributed accountability mechanisms become necessary.

items.title: The Adaptive Waste Management Assistant (AWMA) An IO and IoT-Based Intelligent System for Urban Waste Management
items.abstract: Smart city garbage collection Adaptive Waste Management Assistant (AWMA) is a garbage collection, management service application that integrates the principle of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT) to contribute to the efficiency, precision, and sustainability of the garbage collection procedures. The solutions of the projects address the major issues that the municipalities are experiencing which include the missed garbage collection, incorrect route planning, and improper waste separation and overflowing of garbage bins. The proposed system is based on smart bins with AI assistance in that the devices installed on the bins will have sensors and cameras that will either determine the fill levels, contamination, and sort waste into plastic, paper, metal, and organic materials. Once a bin has reached a specific level, then automatic request of collection is generated and transmitted to a centralized cloud server. The server processes this information and applies the optimal routing algorithms to the close waste collection vehicle to minimize manual labor, prevent overflowing, and have a timely collection process. Real-time monitoring and analytics on data used can assist AWMA in reducing manual labor, preventing overflowing, and ensuring a timely collection process. In addition, the obtained information might be valuable to the municipal government and enable it to forecast, more effectively distribute the resources and work out superior recycling policies. Figma based interface designs and no-code apps were utilised during the prototype stage to serve as a simulation of system functionality. The future developments to the AWMA system include introduction of more advanced machine learning models and a potential of predictive filling patterns, which will demonstrate that the system will shift off of the traditional reactive approach of waste collection and towards a more proactive and automated system. Its architecture is scalable and modular and can be deployed in future in smart cities, college campuses, residential and in business districts. items.title: The Analysis of College Students' Employment Information Management System Based on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Against the backdrop of the widespread application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and big data, the management of college students' employment information faces severe challenges such as data heterogeneity, incomplete information, and low precision in person-job matching. This study proposes a deep learning framework that synergistically integrates Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), attention mechanisms, and Generative Adversarial Network (GAN). The framework is designed based on a key technical insight: local occlusion in image processing is mathematically equivalent to information missing in employment resumes, both involving incomplete representation of input feature vectors. Experiments show that the proposed scheme exhibits remarkable stability and accuracy in intelligent employment recommendation and job matching prediction. Through such cross-domain algorithm validation, this work provides a feasible technical path for the construction of smart employment systems and effectively improves information processing capabilities in complex data environments.

items.title: The Art of (Mis)alignment: How Fine-Tuning Methods Effectively Misalign and Realign LLMs in Post-Training
items.abstract: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) raises significant ethical and safety concerns. While LLM alignment techniques are adopted to improve model safety and trustworthiness, adversaries can exploit these techniques to undermine safety for malicious purposes, resulting in \emph{misalignment}. Misaligned LLMs may be published on open platforms to magnify harm. To address this, additional safety alignment, referred to as \emph{realignment}, is necessary before deploying untrusted third-party LLMs. This study explores the efficacy of fine-tuning methods in terms of misalignment, realignment, and the effects of their interplay. By evaluating four Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and two Preference Fine-Tuning (PFT) methods across four popular safety-aligned LLMs, we reveal a mechanism asymmetry between attack and defense. While Odds Ratio Preference Optimization (ORPO) is most effective for misalignment, Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) excels in realignment, albeit at the expense of model utility. Additionally, we identify model-specific resistance, residual effects of multi-round adversarial dynamics, and other noteworthy findings. These findings highlight the need for robust safeguards and customized safety alignment strategies to mitigate potential risks in the deployment of LLMs. Our code is available at https://github.com/zhangrui4041/The-Art-of-Mis-alignment.

items.title: The augmented recruiter: examining AI integration and decision-making dynamics in Qatar's organisational hiring practices
items.abstract: Purpose This study explored the implementation of artificial intelligence (AI) in recruitment processes within Qatari organisations, focussing on how these technologies impact organisational efficiency, human judgement in decision-making and recruitment outcomes. Design/methodology/approach The research employed an interpretivist philosophy and a case study design, investigating two prominent Qatari firms with contrasting AI recruitment implementation approaches. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with twenty-two participants across various organisational roles and hierarchical levels. The thematic analysis framework was used to identify patterns and relationships within the data. Findings Four key themes emerged, including (1) process optimisation through AI integration, (2) subjectivity in AI-powered recruitment, (3) recruitment strategies in the age of AI and (4) strategic investments in AI. The research found that AI significantly enhanced efficiency through process standardisation and automation, but functioned optimally as an augmentative rather than a replacement technology. Practical implications Organisations should approach AI recruitment tools as augmentative technologies, invest in customisation capabilities, implement comprehensive change management strategies and maintain robust post-hire evaluation procedures. Originality/value The research shifts focus to under-researched non-Western workplace settings, particularly in technologically advancing Middle Eastern economies like Qatar.

items.title: The Cartesian Cut in Agentic AI
items.abstract: LLMs gain competence by predicting words in human text, which often reflects how people perform tasks. Consequently, coupling an LLM to an engineered runtime turns prediction into control: outputs trigger interventions that enact goal-oriented behavior. We argue that a central design lever is where control resides in these systems. Brains embed prediction within layered feedback controllers calibrated by the consequences of action. By contrast, LLM agents implement Cartesian agency: a learned core coupled to an engineered runtime via a symbolic interface that externalizes control state and policies. The split enables bootstrapping, modularity, and governance, but can induce sensitivity and bottlenecks. We outline bounded services, Cartesian agents, and integrated agents as contrasting approaches to control that trade off autonomy, robustness, and oversight.

items.title: The Decentralized AI Ecosystem in Healthcare: A Systematic Review of Technologies, Governance, and Implementation
items.abstract: This research examines the emerging ecosystem of models that are developed and run across a distributed network of computers called decentralized artificial intelligence. The focus is to understand these models in the healthcare context and with a focus on their core components: technologies, governance frameworks, and real-world applications. A systematic literature review was conducted, analyzing peer-reviewed studies from PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science to map the current landscape of the field. The primary objective was to synthesize the current research on decentralized approaches in healthcare, including core approaches like federated learning and blockchain-based AI models, as well as emerging concepts such as agentic AI blockchain-based AI models and DAOs, to comprehend their application in clinical and operational settings. The research assesses the maturity of these implementations, ranging from pilot programs to large-scale organizational settings. It also identified the key computational and technical methods and platforms used and the key benefits and challenges influencing their adoption. The findings underscore the pivotal role of the decentralized paradigm in addressing the fundamental limitations of traditional AI, including data privacy, trust, institutional silos, and regulatory complexity. Insights are also offered for healthcare providers, technology developers, researchers, and policymakers aiming to navigate and leverage decentralized AI to build more equitable, efficient, and collaborative healthcare systems.

items.title: The Double-Edged Sword of Creative Control in Designer-AI Co-Creation with Design Experience as a Boundary Condition
items.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly involved in creative processes, designers encounter a fundamental tension regarding creative control-the degree to which they dominate design direction and iterative decision-making when collaborating with AI. Existing theories offer contradictory predictions: self-determination and psychological ownership theories emphasize the benefits of control, whereas cognitive load theory highlights its cognitive costs. This tension remains empirically unresolved, particularly regarding how designer characteristics shape these competing effects. This study examines the dual-pathway mechanism linking creative control to design creativity and investigates the moderating role of design experience. A scenario-based between-subjects experiment was conducted with 226 designers and design students. Creative control exerted a positive indirect effect on design creativity through psychological ownership (effect = 0.16, 95% CI [0.09, 0.24]) and a negative indirect effect through cognitive load (effect = -0.07, 95% CI [-0.14, -0.02]), confirming the double-edged sword effect. Design experience strengthened the positive pathway while buffering the negative pathway. Creative control thus functions as a double-edged sword in designer-AI co-creation, with its net effect contingent on designer expertise. The results extend Conservation of Resources theory to human-AI collaboration contexts and inform the design of experience-adaptive AI-assisted systems.

items.title: The ecosystem of machine learning competitions: Platforms, participants, and their impact on AI development
items.abstract: Machine learning competitions (MLCs) play a pivotal role in advancing artificial intelligence (AI) by fostering innovation, skill development, and practical problem-solving. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of major competition platforms such as Kaggle and Zindi, examining their workflows, evaluation methodologies, and reward structures. It further assesses competition quality, participant expertise, and global reach, with particular attention to demographic trends among top-performing competitors. By exploring the motivations of competition hosts, this paper underscores the significant role of MLCs in shaping AI development, promoting collaboration, and driving impactful technological progress. Furthermore, by combining literature synthesis with platform-level data analysis and practitioner insights a comprehensive understanding of the MLC ecosystem is provided. Moreover, the paper demonstrates that MLCs function at the intersection of academic research and industrial application, fostering the exchange of knowledge, data, and practical methodologies across domains. Their strong ties to open-source communities further promote collaboration, reproducibility, and continuous innovation within the broader ML ecosystem. By shaping research priorities, informing industry standards, and enabling large-scale crowdsourced problem-solving, these competitions play a key role in the ongoing evolution of AI. The study provides insights relevant to researchers, practitioners, and competition organizers, and includes an examination of the future trajectory and sustained influence of MLCs on AI development.

items.title: The Geometry of Duration and the In-Between — Bergson · Heidegger/Zollikon · Kimura/Kyōto · Corbin/Annales · GI Theory (English edition)
items.abstract: This document is the complete English translation — without any omission or abridgment — of 持続と「あいだ」の幾何学 (The Geometry of Duration and the In-Between). The prose has been written so as to leave no trace of the source language: memoir passages adopt the essayistic register of Isaiah Berlin and George Steiner, mathematical passages the clarity of Michael Atiyah and Roger Penrose, philosophical passages the hermeneutic density of Charles Taylor. The result aspires to the level of a text that could be taken for one composed de novo by an anglophone scholar working in the best tradition of the humanities and the exact sciences alike. The essay investigates the structural resonance — not formal translation, not reduction, but resonance — between four philosophical and historiographical traditions (Bergson's pure duration, Heidegger's existential analytic of Dasein as it unfolded in the Zollikon seminars, Kimura Bin's phenomenological psychiatry of the "in-between" rooted in the Kyōto School, and Alain Corbin's Annales-school history of sensibilities) and the mathematical apparatus of Geometric Intelligence (GI) theory, which constructs data-driven Riemannian manifolds via VAE pullback metrics and performs on these manifolds Lie derivative analysis, curvature tensor computation, geodesic calculation and optimal control. The extended preface situates the author's intellectual formation at the intersection of French philosophy, Russian spirituality, German phenomenology, Japanese thought and mathematical practice — from Saint-Exupéry's Le Petit Prince and Foulquié's philosophy textbook through Bourbaki and Merleau-Ponty's lived body to Chaadayev's Philosophical Letters, Nishida Kitarō's logic of place, the civilisational questions of Turkey, and the structural isomorphism between the founding of Edo, Saint Petersburg and New York. Four chapters examine: (1) Bergson's pure duration and the Lie derivative; (2) the Zollikon seminars and the world as manifold; (3) Kimura Bin's "in-between" and geodesic distance; (4) Corbin's olfactory space and the manifold of sensibility. The epilogue extends to the Langlands programme, Mochizuki's inter-universal Teichmüller theory, Maruyama's categorical unified science, Bronshtein's cGħ cube, and the encounter between Jesuit missionaries and Zen monks in the Azuchi-Momoyama period as a prospective subject for manifold-based empirical historiography. Position of this document within the GI series — the creation of a fourth layer. The publications to date have comprised three layers: Layer 1 (theoretical foundations): GI Theory Vol. 1 (differential-geometric framework) and Vol. 2 (AI Agent · World Models) — what GI theory is. Layer 2 (applications): case studies — Peter the Great (history), the Taiwan Strait (security), the power grid (infrastructure), Ave Verum Corpus (music), a quantitative social science paper (correspondence with existing methods), the history of sensibilities (historiography) — what GI theory can do. Layer 3 (education): forthcoming — Zenn articles (étale sheaves × AI, four levels of mathematical readership from secondary school to graduate school) — how to learn GI theory. This document creates a fourth layer — the philosophical foundations. What GI theory does was shown by Layers 1 and 2. How to teach it was shown by Layer 3. But why GI theory exists — the meaning of its intellectual existence — is spoken for the first time in the present document. That Bergson's pure duration stands in structural resonance with the Lie derivative; that Heidegger's being-in-the-world resonates with embedding on a manifold; that Kimura's "collapse of the in-between" resonates with the plunge of scalar curvature into the negative — these are the philosophical grounds for the claim that GI theory is not a mere mathematical tool but an attempt to describe the structure of human experience. Furthermore, the intellectual autobiography of the preface makes explicit, for the first time in an official publication, the itinerary upon which GI theory was built. From Le Petit Prince to Foulquié, from Bourbaki to Merleau-Ponty, from Heidegger's Fourfold to Russian spirituality — all of these ran beneath GI theory as an underground current, and are now a matter of public record. The complete architecture of the GI series is therefore as follows: Layer 4 (philosophical foundations): this document — why GI theory exists. Layer 1 (theoretical foundations): Vol. 1, Vol. 2 — what GI theory is. Layer 2 (applications): case studies — what GI theory can do. Layer 3 (education): forthcoming — how to learn GI theory (an account of the mathematical world-view through metaphors accessible from secondary school onward). This document is the root of the entire series. All other publications are the trunk, branches and leaves that grow from this root. items.title: The Heart in the Machine: Exploring Digital Empathy and “Artificial Presence” in AI-Supported Relational Teaching
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence becomes more common in today’s educational settings, students started to interact with AI tutors not just as learning tools, but as systems that appear emotionally responsive. This study examines the ideas of digital empathy and artificial presence, how well AI can mimic emotional understanding and a sense of connection, and explores how these factors influence student motivation when compared with traditional human instruction. Using a mixed-methods comparative approach, the study investigates whether an AI tutor’s simulated empathy can maintain student motivation at levels similar to those fostered by a human teacher. Quantitative data on motivation and engagement are combined with qualitative interviews that capture students’ emotional experiences and their sense of connection while learning. In doing so, the study addresses a key tension in modern education, while AI can improve efficiency and offer non-judgmental learning environments, it may also weaken the human relationships that are central to meaningful teaching and learning. The findings aim to guide ethical and thoughtful integration of AI in higher education and contribute to ongoing discussions about relational teaching in the age of intelligent systems. This research advocates for a balanced approach, one in which AI supports instructional tasks, while human educators remain essential for care, mentorship, and genuine human connection to bridge the gap between code and care.

items.title: The Impact of Hybrid Work Arrangements on Employee Productivity and Work-life Balance in the UAE Private Sector
items.abstract: This study examines the impact of hybrid work arrangements on employee productivity and work-life balance in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) private sector with an emphasis on the increasing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in everyday working processes. With hybrid models being more widespread post-COVID-19, UAE organizations have faced challenges concerning flexibility, digital transformation, and employee wellbeing. There is, however, a paucity of research on the functioning of these dynamics in the UAE context in terms of its unique cultural and organizational settings. This gap is filled by the present study, which explores the way workers undergo hybrid work, the way AI technologies help or diminish their work, and the way these two elements influence their general work-life balance. The qualitative design was applied, and 10 employees employed in hybrid positions and using AI tools in various industries of the private sector were interviewed in semi-structured interviews. NVivo software was used to analyze the data thematically to determine the patterns concerning productivity, flexibility, communication, digital fatigue, and AI use. The results indicate that hybrid work increases productivity due to flexibility, lesser time spent, and allowing workers to focus on work during remote workdays. The office days are still significant for teamwork, collaboration, and fast decision-making. The study also revealed issues like a lack of clarity between work and personal life, a gap in communication between employees who work remotely and in-office employees, the fear of AI surveillance, and decreased creativity.

items.title: The impact of regional block presence on large language model–based postoperative analgesia recommendations in abdominal surgery: a comparative study using real-world patient data
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Postoperative pain management is a core component of anesthesiology practice, with regional anesthesia playing a key role in multimodal analgesia strategies. Large language model (LLM)-based artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly proposed as clinical decision support tools; however, their ability to integrate critical perioperative context, such as the presence of an existing regional block, remains insufficiently explored. METHODS: This prospective, observational, comparative study included 144 adult patients undergoing elective abdominal surgery at a tertiary care center, after exclusion of four patients due to severe preoperative or intraoperative complications that significantly altered the planned postoperative analgesia. Patients were grouped according to the presence or absence of a regional block (70 per group). For each patient, anonymized and standardized clinical scenarios were evaluated independently by three LLM-based AI systems (ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot) to generate postoperative analgesia recommendations. AI outputs were assessed by blinded anesthesiology experts for opioid recommendation, multimodal analgesia, consideration of regional anesthesia, and overall clinical appropriateness using a 5-point Likert scale. Multivariable logistic and ordinal logistic regression analyses were performed to determine the independent effect of regional block presence, adjusting for relevant clinical covariates. Agreement between AI recommendations and actual clinical practice was evaluated using Cohen's kappa. RESULTS: Regional block presence was not independently associated with opioid recommendations generated by any AI system (all p > 0.05). However, the likelihood of recommending an additional regional block was significantly reduced by ChatGPT (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.02, p < 0.001) and Copilot (aOR 0.15, p = 0.019). Gemini demonstrated complete separation, consistently recommending regional blocks only in patients without an existing block. Multimodal analgesia was universally recommended by ChatGPT and Gemini, precluding regression analysis. Expert evaluation scores were significantly higher in scenarios with an existing regional block across all AI systems. Overall agreement between AI-generated recommendations and real-world clinical decisions was limited. CONCLUSIONS: LLM-based AI systems demonstrate partial contextual awareness of regional anesthesia when generating postoperative analgesia recommendations. However, this awareness does not consistently translate into concordance with real-world clinical practice. These findings support the use of AI as an adjunctive decision support tool rather than a substitute for clinician judgment in postoperative pain management.

items.title: The Impact of Specific Prompt Engineering Techniques on the Readability of LLM-Generated Patient Materials in Gastroenterology and Hepatology
items.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Health literacy significantly impacts patient outcomes. While the average American reads at an 8th grade reading level, healthcare materials are often written above this, potentially contributing to our nation's health literacy gap. Large language models (LLM) and prompt engineering may be able to help address this gap by consistently generating materials at the recommended 6th grade reading level. Our study aims to assess how different prompting techniques affect the readability of LLM-generated materials. METHODS: We assessed the effects of five prompt techniques (Zero-Shot, Contextualized, Constrained, Meta, Persona) on the readability of LLM-generated explanations for fifteen common gastroenterology and hepatology conditions across twelve LLMs. Output (n = 2655) readability was assessed with two readability metrics (Simple Measure of Gobbledygook (SMOG) index, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL)), followed by significance testing and post-hoc analysis. RESULTS: No prompt technique or model consistently produced outputs at or below a 6th grade reading level when assessed by the SMOG index, the preferred metric when assessing healthcare materials (p < 0.001). However, prompts with less constraints yield less readable outputs, while prompts with more constraints yield significantly more readable outputs (p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the potential of LLMs as a tool in addressing America's health literacy gap, as we show prompt engineering affects the readability of gastroenterology and hepatology-related explanations. We also found limitations to this technique. Further optimization is necessary before LLMs can consistently generate patient materials without appropriate clinician oversight, but it implies prompt engineering as a tool in addressing our nation's health literacy gap.

items.title: The Improvement or Hindrance of the New Generation of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Through relevant theoretical analysis and practical verification, this study aims to reveal the potential impact of the Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer (ChatGPT) on students' critical thinking skills. At the same time, it provides suggestions for the rational application of artificial intelligence (AI) to promote the development of critical thinking. Thus, it can offer references for ChatGPT's sustainable development and application scope expansion. The study adopts a combination of quantitative and qualitative methods, constructs multi-dimensional indicator calculation equations, and integrates students' subjective experiences. Meanwhile, it uses public databases such as the Education Resources Information Center (ERIC), Web of Science, Scopus, and IEEE Xplore to evaluate different versions of ChatGPT. The study shows that ChatGPT positively impacts students' critical thinking skills in higher education and can effectively help students build a rational thinking system.

items.title: The Interactive Design Process Framework (IDPF): Utilizing GenAI as a Collaborative Agent for Creating STEAM Projects
items.abstract: Increasingly, teachers are considering using Generative AI (GenAI) and large language models (LLMs) as new tools for developing lessons and creating resources. Interdisciplinary STEAM project design specifically continues to be problematic because it requires many professionals to work together in integrative ways when developing successful STEAM project designs. Collaborating closely to develop authentic problems, establish a high level of pedagogical quality, use principles of inclusive design, and create valid and reliable assessment instruments often exceeds the individual teacher’s professional expertise and available time. The purpose of this conceptual paper is to lay the foundation of what we call “the Interactive Design Process Framework (IDPF)” and propose its use in instruction. IDPF has four steps: Co-design, Analysis, Expert Review, and Synthesis. Using these four iterative (cyclical) steps, the IDPF framework positions GenAI as a collaborative designer to work with both classroom teachers and subject area expert reviewers. As a conceptual contribution, this paper does not present empirical data; rather, it articulates the theoretical rationale, structural logic, and design principles of the framework as a foundation for future empirical investigation. In addition to a primary education example of illustration, implications for practice, limitations of the study, and recommendations for future research are discussed.

items.title: The Last War Philosophical Insights into the End of Humanity
items.abstract: The history of human civilization has been shaped by war, each conflict etching its legacy into the fabric of existence. Yet, what if the final war, the one that concludes the saga of humanity, is upon us? In this thought-provoking exploration, Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, delves into the philosophical, ethical, and existential implications of humanity’s last war. This book does not merely examine warfare as a strategic or political tool but questions its role in defining human identity. As technological advancements in weaponry accelerate toward an uncontrollable abyss, the line between self-defense and self-destruction blurs. From the ethical dilemmas of nuclear warfare to the digital battlegrounds of the future, every chapter illuminates the fragility of peace and the looming shadow of extinction. By weaving historical analysis, philosophical reflections, and contemporary case studies, this work serves as both a warning and an inquiry. Can war be averted, or is it an inevitable conclusion to human nature? What moral responsibilities do global leaders bear in preventing such devastation? With deep intellectual rigor and an urgent sense of realism, this book invites readers to confront the possibility of the last war—not as a distant nightmare but as a stark reality demanding immediate contemplation. The writing of this book is deeply rooted in the concern that modern warfare has evolved beyond conventional understanding. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, authored this work in response to the alarming trajectory of global conflicts that now intertwine with technological singularity, artificial intelligence, and weapons of unprecedented destruction. Published in 2011, this study aims to dissect the philosophical dimensions of war, highlighting the paradox of progress that brings humanity closer to its ultimate demise. War has long been perceived as a mechanism of power, control, and territorial expansion. However, this book redefines conflict not as an isolated event but as a culmination of human ideologies, fears, and the relentless pursuit of superiority. The discussion extends beyond conventional military strategies, touching upon cyberwarfare, biological weapons, and AI-driven conflicts, emphasizing the urgency of ethical governance over technological advancements. The rapid militarization of space, the increasing automation of warfare, and the unpredictable nature of geopolitical tensions have necessitated a deeper inquiry into the finality of war. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, observed that humanity stands at a critical threshold where the distinction between war and annihilation is vanishing. The rise of unmanned combat systems and autonomous decision-making weapons amplifies the risk of irreversible global catastrophe. The central theme of this book is the philosophical interrogation of war's necessity and its ethical ramifications. Through existentialist and utilitarian perspectives, the book scrutinizes whether human civilization can exist without conflict or if war is embedded in the very essence of human survival. The exploration is not limited to military confrontations but extends to socio-political conflicts, ideological warfare, and economic battles that shape global stability. While wars of the past have followed discernible patterns, modern warfare presents unpredictability fueled by technological dominance. The book identifies economic disparity, resource depletion, and political radicalization as harbingers of the last war. These indicators serve as a warning system for humanity, urging proactive measures before irreversible escalation. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, establishes multiple variables essential for understanding war’s trajectory, including state sovereignty, military-industrial expansion, ethical considerations in AI warfare, and the psychological conditioning of societies toward conflict acceptance. By analyzing these elements, the book constructs a framework to predict and possibly mitigate future large-scale wars. Several key factors drive the discussion within this book: the historical repetition of wars despite peace efforts, the weaponization of emerging technologies, and the philosophical dilemma of whether war is an unavoidable consequence of civilization. The study also considers the role of global governance institutions and their effectiveness in preventing mass destruction. The work presents theoretical and practical approaches to conflict resolution, advocating for diplomatic restructuring, ethical AI governance, and alternative frameworks for international negotiations. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, proposes a shift in global priorities—from military investment to sustainable human development—as a critical strategy in averting global catastrophe. The path toward eradicating war is fraught with challenges, including political resistance, economic dependencies on warfare industries, and the psychological normalization of conflict. While international organizations and peace movements provide counterbalances, the overwhelming momentum of military expansion presents a formidable obstacle to lasting peace. In summarizing the philosophical inquiry into the last war, this book serves as a stark reminder of the fragility of civilization. It posits that the final war is not an abstract fear but a plausible outcome if humanity fails to reassess its approach to power, aggression, and technological development. Through this reflective journey, Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, urges leaders, thinkers, and global citizens to engage in deeper discourse on the ethical and existential stakes of continued warfare.

items.title: The Longitudinal Relationship Between Intrinsic Motivation, Grade Motivation and Prosocial Behavior in Chinese Adolescents: A Cross-Lagged Panel Study
items.abstract: Prosocial behavior is crucial for the development of adolescents. Prosocial behavior requires strong internal motivation to drive it, but the prospective association between the two is still unclear. In addition, there is still a gap in the relationship between grade motivation as a unique external motivation and prosocial behavior. To explore the prospective associations between them, we conducted two follow-up surveys (six months apart) on 862 Chinese adolescents (423 boys and 439 girls) to collect data on intrinsic motivation, grade motivation and prosocial behavior (relational prosocial behavior and practical prosocial behavior). The cross-lagged panel study results revealed that intrinsic motivation at T1 was positively associated with relational and practical prosocial behavior at T2. In contrast, grade motivation at T1 was not significantly associated with later prosocial behavior, and prosocial behavior at T1 was not significantly associated with later intrinsic motivation or grade motivation. These findings indicate that intrinsic motivation may be a potential antecedent for prosocial behavior in Chinese adolescents later in life, but the observed associations should be cautiously interpreted.
topics: Child and Adolescent Psychosocial and Emotional Development

items.title: The moderating role of gender and generational cohort on the effects of artificial intelligence usage and learning adaptability on the academic performance of university students in Zimbabwe
items.abstract: This study investigated the moderating role of gender and generational cohorts on the effects of artificial intelligence (AI) usage, learning adaptability, and academic performance of university students in Zimbabwe. Three hundred and twenty-five students at Great Zimbabwe University, Zimbabwe Open University and Women's University in Africa responded to the questionnaires. The study found that AI usage and learning adaptability positively effect academic performance. The study found that generational cohort moderates the effects of AI usage on academic performance, but gender does not. The findings of this research are that gender and generational cohort do not moderate the effects of learning adaptability and academic performance of university students in Zimbabwe. The research implies that students should use AI to enhance their academic performance and develop learning adaptability, which is also key to academic performance.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

items.title: The moon’s many faces: A single unified transformer for multimodal lunar reconstruction
items.abstract: Multimodal learning is an emerging research topic across multiple disciplines but has rarely been applied to planetary science. In this contribution, we propose a single, unified transformer architecture trained to learn shared representations between multiple sources like grayscale images, Digital Elevation Models (DEMs), surface normals, and albedo maps. The architecture supports flexible translation from any input modality to any target modality. Our results demonstrate that our foundation model learns physically plausible relations across these four modalities. We further identify that image-based 3D reconstruction and albedo estimation (Shape and Albedo from Shading) of lunar images can be formulated as a multimodal learning problem. Our results demonstrate the potential of multimodal learning to solve Shape and Albedo from Shading and provide a new approach for large-scale planetary 3D reconstruction. Adding more input modalities in the future will further improve the results and enable tasks such as photometric normalization and co-registration.

items.title: The need for verification in artificial intelligence-driven scientific discovery
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the practice of science. Machine learning (ML) and large language models (LLMs) can generate hypotheses at a scale and speed far exceeding traditional methods, offering the potential to accelerate discovery across diverse fields. However, the abundance of hypotheses introduces a critical challenge; without scalable and reliable mechanisms for verification, scientific progress risks being hindered rather than advanced. In this article, we trace the historical development of scientific discovery, examine how AI is reshaping established practices for discovery and review the principal approaches, ranging from data-driven methods and knowledge-aware neural architectures to symbolic reasoning frameworks and LLM agents. While these systems can uncover patterns and propose candidate laws, their scientific value ultimately depends on rigorous and transparent verification, which we argue must be the cornerstone of AI-assisted discovery. This article is part of the discussion meeting issue 'Symbolic regression in the physical sciences'.

items.title: THE PARADOX OF IRRIGATED FRUIT CULTURE: SOCIOENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS AND OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH IN THE PETROLINA-JUAZEIRO HUB
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of irrigated fruit production in the Petrolina–Juazeiro hub has positioned the Brazilian semiarid as a strategic agro-export region, while simultaneously intensifying socioenvironmental inequalities and occupational health risks. This paradox reflects a development model in which economic gains coexist with diffuse and often invisible forms of exposure. This study aims to analyze the socioenvironmental and health impacts associated with irrigated agribusiness, focusing on the interaction between chemical exposure, water dynamics, and territorial vulnerability. An integrative literature review was conducted using international and regional databases, complemented by grey literature. A total of 216 records were initially identified and subjected to systematic screening and eligibility procedures. The analysis was structured around three axes: biochemical-clinical, socioeconomic, and geoenvironmental. The results indicate that pesticide exposure in the region is chronic, cumulative, and mediated by environmental and social factors. Evidence shows associations with genotoxicity, endocrine disruption, and underreported chronic diseases, alongside labor precariousness and gender inequality. Contamination pathways extend through soil and water systems, amplifying exposure beyond occupational settings. The discussion reveals that these dynamics are embedded in a broader framework of environmental injustice, where risks are unevenly distributed and structurally produced. The interaction between climate conditions, irrigation systems, and chemical use intensifies exposure, supporting the conceptualization of a chemical-hydric exposome. In conclusion, the study highlights the need for integrated regulatory approaches, improved surveillance systems, and policies that address cumulative exposure and territorial inequalities in semiarid agro-export regions.

items.title: The Political Philosophy of War Propaganda and Its Consequences
items.abstract: War is not merely fought with weapons on the battlefield but is shaped long before the first shot is fired. 2011. The Political Philosophy of War Propaganda and Its Consequences is a profound exploration of how propaganda has been systematically used to manipulate perceptions, justify conflicts, and sustain power structures. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, unveils the intricate relationship between war narratives, state agendas, and the psychological conditioning of societies. Published in 2011 in Geneva, Switzerland, this book critically examines the philosophy underpinning propaganda and its far-reaching implications. The pages unravel historical and contemporary examples of war propaganda, shedding light on how information is weaponized to manufacture consent. Governments, media, and international institutions are dissected as the architects of public opinion, often distorting reality to serve political and economic interests. The book further explores how the United Nations, as a global entity, struggles to navigate these deceptive narratives while attempting to maintain peace and diplomacy. Education is presented as both a battleground and a tool for resistance. The Education Training Centre is examined as a potential counterforce against the institutionalized manipulation of truth. By fostering critical thinking and ethical discourse, societies can reclaim their agency and dismantle the illusions that perpetuate endless cycles of war. This book is a wake-up call—an urgent appeal to question, analyze, and resist the forces that dictate the course of global conflict. The motivation for writing this book arises from the undeniable impact of propaganda in shaping wars and their aftermath. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, seeks to unravel the mechanisms that allow propaganda to thrive and its role in constructing war as a necessary, even heroic, endeavor. The book was published in 2011 in Geneva, Switzerland, a city renowned for its diplomatic engagements and as a hub of international discourse on peace and conflict. History has repeatedly demonstrated that wars are not only fought with military power but also with narratives that legitimize aggression. From ancient empires to modern superpowers, states have mastered the art of persuasion to justify violence, rally populations, and silence opposition. This book challenges these accepted truths, urging readers to dissect the real motivations behind global conflicts. To understand the philosophy of war propaganda, Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, defines key concepts such as "manufactured consent," "psychological warfare," and "strategic misinformation." The book provides an analytical framework to decipher how propaganda functions across different political systems and historical periods. Truth becomes a malleable instrument in the hands of those who control information. The book dissects how linguistic framing, emotional appeal, and repetition are used to construct compelling war narratives that suppress critical thinking and pacify opposition. The modern world presents an evolution in propaganda techniques. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, highlights the role of digital warfare, social media manipulation, and the emergence of artificial intelligence-driven disinformation campaigns. Governments and non-state actors alike now have unprecedented tools to shape perceptions on a global scale. Case studies illustrate how recent conflicts have been fueled by misinformation, fabricated threats, and the demonization of opponents. The book presents chilling examples of how media, once seen as a guardian of truth, often becomes complicit in amplifying war rhetoric. This book is built upon principles that deconstruct the political philosophy of propaganda. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, adopts an interdisciplinary approach, integrating political science, psychology, and media studies to expose how war narratives are crafted and sustained. Through a comparative analysis of historical and contemporary conflicts, the book establishes a framework to recognize and challenge propaganda in real time. The goal is not just to understand the phenomenon but to empower individuals and institutions to resist its influence. To assess the presence and impact of war propaganda, this book identifies recurring indicators, including: • The deliberate distortion of facts to justify military action. • The portrayal of war as an act of moral duty or national survival. • The suppression of dissenting voices through censorship or intimidation. • The glorification of military actions while downplaying civilian casualties. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, meticulously examines these elements, providing readers with analytical tools to recognize propaganda before it takes hold. The effectiveness of war propaganda is influenced by several operational variables, which include state control over media, public education, and ideological indoctrination. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, reveals how these variables intersect to create a cohesive and persuasive narrative that discourages critical scrutiny. A crucial aspect of this analysis is the role of education as both a target and a solution. The book explores how school curricula, history books, and public discourse shape perceptions of war from an early age. The persistence of war propaganda is driven by key determinant factors such as: • The geopolitical interests of states seeking to expand influence. • The economic benefits of sustained military conflicts. • The ideological rivalries that create perpetual divisions. • The complicity of mass media in disseminating misleading information. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, argues that these factors create a self-reinforcing system that ensures propaganda remains a powerful force in global politics. While propaganda is deeply entrenched in political structures, strategies exist to counter its effects. The book proposes reforms in education, media literacy programs, and international regulations on misinformation. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, emphasizes the importance of academic institutions and global organizations in fostering a more informed and critically engaged society. The role of The Education Training Centre is examined as a model for institutions dedicated to cultivating critical thinking and resistance to manipulative narratives. Efforts to dismantle propaganda face resistance from state entities, corporate media interests, and political ideologues who benefit from maintaining control over information. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, acknowledges these challenges while also highlighting the growing movement of independent journalism and grassroots educational initiatives pushing back against misinformation. The book closes with a sobering yet hopeful message. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, asserts that propaganda will always exist, but its power depends on the willingness of societies to accept it without question. By cultivating skepticism, promoting transparency, and demanding accountability, humanity can reclaim its autonomy from those who seek to manipulate truth for political gain.

items.title: The Potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a Proactive Tool in Public Health Surveillance
items.abstract: COVID-19 exposed structural fragilities in the United States' public health logistics and supply chain systems, particularly in the domains of diagnostic testing, epidemiological tracking, and coordinated response. These deficiencies underscore the urgent need for more adaptive, data-centric surveillance infrastructures capable of operating at scale and in real time. Artificial intelligence–enabled analytics, when integrated with existing public health systems, offer a viable pathway to enhance situational awareness, optimize resource allocation, and improve the timeliness of intervention strategies. In particular, wastewater-based epidemiology; augmented by AI-driven pattern recognition and predictive modeling; presents a scalable and cost-effective mechanism for population-level health monitoring, capable of detecting emerging threats prior to clinical reporting. This study advances that premise by examining how such integrative approaches can strengthen logistical decision-making and supply chain responsiveness.

items.title: THE POTENTIAL OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR RUSSIAN HIGHER EDUCATION
items.abstract: This article examines the use of artificial intelligence in higher education institutions. It demonstrates that a key advantage of AI for universities is its potential to personalize learning. This is crucial given the diversity of learning styles, learning speeds, and professional ambitions of today's students. Smart analytics platforms, by processing data on each student's academic performance, preferences, and typical difficulties, can create personalized educational paths. This method allows students to work with material that best meets their individual needs. This allows for in-depth mastery of complex topics and rapid review of previous learning. Expanding access to knowledge is another important benefit brought about by artificial intelligence technologies. Digital educational environments, intelligent assistants, and translation and text creation tools make learning accessible to individuals with disabilities, those living in remote areas, and those who combine education with work or family responsibilities. AI helps overcome geographic and physical barriers, facilitating the globalization of quality higher education.

items.title: The Proactive Paradigm: Leveraging Multi-Agent AI Systems for Autonomous Network Operations
items.abstract: The scale, complexity, and traffic dynamism of contemporary network environments have outpaced what threshold-based alerting systems and human-led monitoring approaches can reliably manage. Reactive paradigms that register conditions only after they have materialized leave organizations continuously exposed to service downtime and degraded user experiences that carry measurable operational and financial consequences. This article presents an architectural framework for proactive network operations organized around a multi-agent artificial intelligence system. Network intelligence is distributed across four functionally distinct agent classes- Collector, Analyst, Resolver, and Coordinator—operating collectively to monitor, analyze, predict, and intervene before network conditions reach the service impact threshold. The Analyst Agent layer draws on four AI model types, each selected for the specific analytical demands of its designated function: recurrent neural networks for predictive time-series analysis, graph neural networks for topological dependency modeling, reinforcement learning for dynamic traffic engineering optimization, and large language models for root cause analysis from unstructured log data. A Network Digital Twin provides the training, simulation, and validation environment through which autonomous action is tested and confirmed before any intervention reaches the production network. The framework advances from reactive troubleshooting toward a proactive, AI-driven network assurance model, offering organizations a structured pathway to self-healing infrastructure grounded in architectural principles rather than speculative capability projections.

items.title: THE PROBLEM OF ENSURING HUMAN RIGHTS IN THE CONTEXT OF TRANSFORMATION TO A DIGITAL SOCIETY
items.abstract: The rapid shift toward a digital society has significantly transformed the way individuals interact, communicate, and access information. While digitalization creates new opportunities for economic growth, education, and social participation, it also introduces complex challenges related to the protection and realization of human rights. This study explores the key issues surrounding the safeguarding of human rights in the context of digital transformation, focusing on privacy, data protection, freedom of expression, and digital inequality. The research analyzes how emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and big data, influence the balance between security and individual freedoms. Furthermore, it highlights the risks of surveillance, cyber threats, and unequal access to digital resources, which may lead to new forms of discrimination and exclusion. The paper emphasizes the necessity of developing effective legal frameworks, ethical standards, and international cooperation mechanisms to ensure that digital progress does not undermine fundamental human rights. The findings suggest that a human-centered approach to digital development is essential for creating an inclusive and rights-respecting digital society.
